title: How does Text 2 relate to Text 1?
subtitle: Cross-Text Connections · 16 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **16 of the official questions in Cross-Text Connections are this one** — 4 Easy, 5 Medium, 7 Hard.
Most versions sit at the Hard tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The question asks which choice best describes how Text 2 relates to Text 1, or how Text 1 would respond to Text 2 (the reversed direction).

- The choices describe what one text does to the other: 'offers a specific example of the general problem in Text 1', 'provides evidence that supports...', 'proposes an alternative explanation for...', 'applies the concept to a different field'.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Name what each text does in one abstract verb phrase: Text 1 'states a general benefit', Text 2 'shows a field lacking it'.
- 2) Name the link between them: example of, contrast to, extension of, or challenge to.
- 3) Match the choice whose structure fits both halves, and check the direction the question asks about (Text 1 on Text 2 or Text 2 on Text 1).

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You read it as 'Text 2 responds to Text 1' when the question asks the reverse, or when the texts are parallel and neither mentions the other.
Also watch for choices that get one text's role right and the other's wrong.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
You read it as 'Text 2 responds to Text 1' when the question asks the reverse, or when the texts are parallel and neither mentions the other.
Also watch for choices that get one text's role right and the other's wrong.
